extracted.intended_audience: prospective grantees, advisors, and partners seeking funding from Klingenstein Philanthropies
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the foundation's mission, programmatic focus areas, and the values/expectations that guide its funding decisions (what the foundation prioritizes, the types of work it supports, and its preferred approach to engagement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Klingenstein Philanthropies focuses its work on neuroscience, children’s health, early literacy, and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should align proposals with one or more of these core focus areas; the homepage repeatedly frames the foundation’s activity and featured grantees around these topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for breakthrough neuroscience research
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting breakthrough research in basic and clinical neuroscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation is committed to investing in 'breakthrough neuroscience research'—preference indicated for research that advances understanding and treatment in neuroscience rather than incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children’s mental health priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeking to improve the understanding and treatment of child and adolescent ADHD and depression, and to improve access to mental health care for children and their families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that address prevention and treatment of ADHD and depression or that improve access to care for children and families are within scope for the Children’s Mental Health work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early childhood mental health and well-being
rubrics_metrics.description: Improving the mental health and well‑being of young children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives targeting the early childhood period and aiming to improve young children's mental health are emphasized across the foundation’s early childhood activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early literacy goal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should contribute to measurable improvements in early literacy; the foundation explicitly names universal reading ability as an objective for its early literacy work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment / climate mitigation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental grants are oriented toward community-level climate mitigation efforts rather than unrelated environmental topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children’s oral health in Maine
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancing the health of Maine’s children, especially their oral health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation has a geographically targeted commitment (Maine) for children’s oral health—applicants working in this domain and geography are particularly relevant to that program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for measurable results and scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: The family has valued 'scientific research' and 'measurable results' as guiding principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that include rigorous evidence, measurable outcomes, and research-based approaches are more likely to align with the foundation’s expectations; the homepage emphasizes measurable results as a core value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term commitment and patience
rubrics_metrics.description: The areas we commit to are challenging and do not lend themselves to easy answers or quick fixes. They require patience and a long-term perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation prefers sustained engagement—once it decides to get involved in a field it 'tends to stay the course'—so applicants should propose work that anticipates multi-year partnership/impact horizons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of expert advice and advisory committees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Klingenstein family values 'the advice of experts' and maintains Scientific Advisory Committees and Advisory Committees for program areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation consults experts in its program areas; proposals that are informed by or connected to expert knowledge, advisory input, or credible scientific/clinical advisory bodies will resonate with this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for scaling effective models
rubrics_metrics.description: Example grantee work includes supporting HealthySteps to build and launch an Expert Faculty program to help scale the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation demonstrates interest in activities that scale evidence-based or promising program models; applicants proposing scalable interventions or capacity-building for scale should highlight that component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest in innovative methods and predictive approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Featured work includes examining application of a predictive model to prevent suicide in Native American youth (NATIVE-RISE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation is open to innovative, data-driven approaches (e.g., predictive models) especially when targeted at high-need populations—applications employing novel methods should clearly articulate their validity and ethical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on partnerships and working with communities/partners
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘We’re grateful for our partners in neuroscience, children’s health, and independent education.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation works through and alongside partners; proposals that demonstrate strong partnerships, community engagement, or collaboration with established organizations are consistent with the foundation’s practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific application pathways (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The site structures 'Applying' pages under specific program areas (Neuroscience → Applying; Early Childhood → Overview and Grantees; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the program-specific 'Applying' pages for each focus area—eligibility, application processes, and priorities may differ by program rather than being uniform across the foundation.
